purpose: Compare static and gaze-contingent visual policies in a synthetic playback before any desktop overlay.

activities.label: verify protected peripheral policy against static and unprotected controls

queries.question: Can VIZZ reduce low-priority peripheral detail while preserving a peripheral alert in a controlled playback?

assumptions: The screen angular extent is a declared playback fixture, not an individual measurement.
Peripheral signals are marked by the synthetic scene designer and are not inferred from human attention.
A policy descriptor is not yet a production renderer.
kill_tests: Protected adaptive mode must preserve the synthetic peripheral alert.
The unprotected control must expose the failure mode by degrading that alert.
Static full mode must not alter detail.
The playback must not open a camera or mutate the desktop.
unknowns: Whether humans notice or prefer the protected policy.
How latency and gaze error alter the safe radii in real use.
Whether the same policy transfers across reading, coding and monitoring.
